article_sentences: Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Minister Nimmala Ramanaidu has directed irrigation officials to remain on high alert in view of heavy rainfall triggered by Cyclone Murasu and take immediate steps to drain rainwater stagnating in agricultural fields to prevent further damage to crops.

During a teleconference with senior irrigation officials on Wednesday (November 4, 2026), the Minister called for continuous monitoring of flood flows in rivers, streams, drains and reservoirs and coordination with other departments to manage the situation.
The Minister said heavy rainfall had been reported in Palnadu, Guntur, Bapatla, Prakasam, Krishna, Eluru and West Godavari districts.
The Nallamada and Parchur drains were flowing above their maximum levels in areas around Parchur, Bapatla, Chirala and Prattipadu.
He asked officials to remain vigilant and take precautionary measures.
Mr. Ramanaidu directed officials to ensure that rainwater accumulated in agricultural fields was drained immediately through canals and drains.
He also asked them to monitor field conditions continuously and ensure that farmers did not face difficulties.

He instructed officials to keep a close watch on flood inflows into the Budameru, Errakalava, Goneruvagu, Tammileru and Yeleru rivers and streams, as well as reservoirs, particularly in view of heavy rainfall in their upstream catchments.
The Minister said the Prakasam Barrage was receiving an inflow of 71,000 cusecs from streams in Guntur and Palnadu districts.
Water from the Budameru catchment was being diverted into the Krishna through the Budameru Diversion Canal, he added.
He called for continuous monitoring of inflows into the Prakasam Barrage and effective flood management.
Referring to the heavy rainfall in Vijayawada over the past two days, Mr. Ramanaidu said 3,000 cusecs of water was being diverted into the sea through the Enikepadu under-tunnel.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court has issued notice on a public interest litigation challenging the constitutional validity of Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023.

The provision grants the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and Election Commissioners immunity from legal proceedings for acts performed or decisions taken in their official capacity during their tenure.
A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought responses on the petition filed by activist and lawyer Arun Kumar Agrawal.
The petitioner has argued that Section 16 provides blanket protection without specifying exceptions for actions allegedly carried out in bad faith or beyond the officials' legal authority.
The plea contends that such immunity limits citizens' access to civil and criminal remedies against members of the Election Commission.
The petition also argues that protecting the independence of the Election Commission should not mean removing accountability for its officials.
It has asked the court to declare Section 16 unconstitutional.
The development came during a separate hearing on petitions challenging the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
During the SIR hearing, the bench questioned the Election Commission about the urgency and implementation of the revision exercise.
It asked whether the process had been designed to harass or intimidate voters and questioned the need to conduct it in Delhi when no election was imminent.

stories.headline: “Public Office Not Consolation Prize For Defeated Politician”: Karnataka High Court Quashes Committee Headed By Congress Leader Who Lost Election
stories.title: “Public Office Not Consolation Prize For Defeated Politician”: Karnataka High Court Quashes Committee Headed By Congress Leader Who Lost Election
stories.summary: Desire to rehabilitate a leader who lost political ground can't justify creating an additional position, Court said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Desire to rehabilitate a leader who lost political ground can't justify creating an additional position, Court said.
The Karnataka High Court on Monday asked the state government to not treat a public office as a “consolation prize for a defeated politician” or a “reward for political loyalty.”

The Court made these stern remarks while setting aside the notifications through which K. Gopal Poojary— an Indian National Congress candidate who lost the 2023 state assembly elections from Byndoor constituency— was appointed as the chairman of the additional land regularisation committee.

“A personal request, political influence or the desire to rehabilitate a leader who has lost political ground cannot, by itself, furnish a justification for creating an additional position or arrangement.

The circumstances suggest an attempt to secure a position of authority through an indirect route and to regain power through a back-door route, rather than to address any genuine public necessity… The desire of an individual to cling on to power cannot be permitted to dictate the course of public administration,” the Bench of Justice D.K. Singh and H. Shanthi Bhushan said.

“The State Government must, therefore, remain above considerations of personal political advancement and ensure that its decisions are guided by public interest and genuine administrative necessity, rather than by an attempt to accommodate an individual's desire to regain lost authority,” the Bench advised.

The present appeal before the Division Bench was filed by Gururaj Gantihole, an MLA from the Byndoor constituency and chairman of the regularisation committee for land grants as per Section 94-A(1) of the Karnataka Land Revenue Act.
He challenged the Single Judge order which had dismissed his petition against two notifications.
The first notification, dated December 4, 2023, constituted an additional land regularisation committee and appointed Poojary as its chairman.

The second notification, dated December 26, 2023, allocated nearly twice as many pending applications (23,983 applications) to the Additional Committee compared to the appellant's committee (12,313 applications).
The appellant had also challenged the constitutional validity of Rule 108-EE of the Karnataka Land Revenue Rules, 1966 in his petition.
Under the Act, an additional land regularisation committee can be formed if the government is of the opinion that constitution of an additional panel is necessary.

stories.headline: Cabinet clears Viksit Bharat Initiative (VISTAR) to strengthen statistical systems, analytics and research from 2026-27 to 2030-31
stories.title: Cabinet clears Viksit Bharat Initiative (VISTAR) to strengthen statistical systems, analytics and research from 2026-27 to 2030-31
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 04: The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, today approved the ‘Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics & Research (VISTAR)’ Scheme for the period FY 2026-27 to FY 2030-31 with an outlay of Rs.4,371.10 crore. Aligned with the central objective of Viksit Bharat 2047, the VISTAR Scheme is designed to establish a dynamic, real-time and future-ready official statistical architecture for enhanced timeliness, data granularity, interoperability with harmonised and AI ready datasets. The VISTAR scheme will provide the strategic flexibility to dynamically allocate resources based on immediate policy needs, fostering a holistic approach to large-scale survey execution, methodological research, digital transformation, and national data governance. VISTAR Scheme will encompass all statistical and data management activities of MoSPI and it will play a crucial role for upgrading the official statistical system of the country. The three components of the VISTAR scheme are as follows: Component 1: Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem; Component 2: Support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS); and Component 3: Economic Census (EC) Under the Comprehensive Statistical Operations and Strengthening of Ecosystem component, MoSPI proposes conducting 59 surveys during the 16th FC cycle, as compared to 43 major surveys conducted previously, potentially filling up critical data gaps in various sectors, thereby, improving decision-making and enabling timely and targeted policy interventions. In addition, building on recent digital transformations in technology enabled data collection and user-centric dissemination, MoSPI will focus on the end-to-end digitalization of statistical processes and embedding Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning into regular workflows, primarily for data processing, validation, and analysis. MoSPI is planning to release new metrices, including the Headline Index of Services Production, the Index of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises. MoSPI will build upon the foundational pillars of data harmonisation such as data cataloguing, machine readability, interoperability, sharing protocols, and privacy by design etc. to dismantle silos and improve programme targeting, reduce duplication, and pave the way for AI-driven decision-making across government levels. By mainstreaming alternate sources—like mobile phone, scanner, and e-commerce data—MoSPI will aim to complement traditional surveys, reduce respondent burden, fill data gaps, and strengthen evidence-based policymaking. Furthermore, MoSPI will ensure capacity building and enhanced opportunities for youth and researchers through Internship Scheme for students and research proposals from academic & research institutions. Under the Support for Statistical Strengthening (SSS) component, funds are to be provided to State/UT Governments for transforming the statistical capabilities of States and Union Territories through a redesigned, deliverable-linked framework (SSS 2.0). The vision focuses on building state-level capacity to generate high-quality, granular data at the district and other disaggregated levels, developing indigenous data processing capabilities, and embedding data use cases into localized policymaking. MoSPI will provide technical support to scale up generation of district-level estimates and million-plus city level estimates in flagship national surveys (e.g., PLFS, HCES, ASUSE) as well as in compilation of State/District level GDP and State level IIP. Under the Economic Census (EC) component, MoSPI will undertake the 8th Economic Census (EC) in collaboration with the States / UTs which will provide granular data and activity details of all the non – farm establishments and workers hired, therein, upto Gram Panchayat and Ward level, providing an assessment of the unorganized sector of the economy and will serve as the baseline for developing National Statistical Business Register (SBR) to facilitate targeted enterprise surveys and strategic interventions. The economic census data will be extremely useful for planners and policy makers at national and sub-national levels, which will pave way for estimating the contribution of unorganized sector to the Gross Domestic Product (GDP).

Prohibitory orders, detentions and the removal of a protest site are exactly the measures the Constitution asks courts to test for proportionality.

stories.headline: ISA Report Makes Case For Achieving 888 GWh of Energy Storage by 2035–36 In India
stories.title: ISA Report Makes Case For Achieving 888 GWh of Energy Storage by 2035–36 In India
stories.summary: India will require 888 GWh of energy storage capacity by 2035–36 to support its expanding renewable energy base and maintain grid reliability, according to the report India’s Energy Storage by the International Solar Alliance (ISA). The report identifies project execution, financing, market development, domestic manufacturing and regulatory coordination as key factors that will determine whether the country can meet its growing storage requirements. The Central Electricity Authority’s (CEA) projections indicate that the requirement comprises 321 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems ( BESS ) and 567 GWh of Pumped Storage Projects (PSP). The report also outlines a requirement of 2,380 GWh by 2047 under its stated scenario, in line with the country’s broader Viksit Bharat 2047 ambitions. The report highlights that while India has made progress in establishing a policy framework for energy storage, the next phase will depend on converting procurement activity into commissioned projects and creating a commercially sustainable ecosystem. It calls for coordinated action across planning, regulation, investment, grid integration and manufacturing to accelerate deployment. Execution and Market Reforms Key to Scaling Storage A key concern highlighted in the report is the gap between energy storage tenders and their conversion into operational assets. Although India has pursued tenders for Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE), solar projects combined with BESS, and standalone battery storage, the conversion of awarded capacity into Power Sale Agreements has remained a challenge. The report recommends moving beyond single application procurement models focused primarily on energy arbitrage. Future tender structures, it says, should incorporate multiple revenue streams, capacity support provisions and stronger enforcement mechanisms for Power Sale Agreements. It also calls for the development of market mechanisms that allow storage assets to participate in ancillary services and other grid support functions. Revenue stacking, which enables storage projects to earn from multiple applications, is identified as an important step towards reducing dependence on government support and improving project viability. Three Scenarios Map India's Storage Deployment Path The report presents three possible deployment scenarios: Policy as Stated, Accelerated and Constrained. These account for differences in policy implementation, investment, technology adoption, manufacturing growth and project execution. Under the Policy as Stated scenario, India's storage requirement is projected at 888 GWh by 2035–36 and 2,380 GWh by 2047. The Accelerated scenario estimates that capacity could reach 1,000–1,150 GWh by 2035–36 and 3,000–3,500 GWh by 2047, supported by faster project execution, stronger investment, revenue stacking and domestic manufacturing. The report clarifies that these are scenario based estimates rather than official targets. It also notes that a definitive 2070 storage projection would require further modelling, given the uncertainty surrounding future technology costs, policy continuity and global supply chains. Report Sets Out Phased Actions Through 2070 The report's recommendations are organised across immediate, near term, medium term and long term priorities. Actions proposed by 2027 include strengthening certification and enforcement, resolving classification related ambiguity for containerised BESS, mandating grid forming inverters in new BESS tenders and completing the allocation of the second tranche of Viability Gap Funding. For 2027 to 2030, the focus shifts to enabling revenue stacking, opening ancillary services to storage, reforming Energy Storage Obligations through state specific targets and establishing a regulatory framework for behind the meter storage. The report also recommends setting up a National Energy Storage Testing Centre. Between 2030 and 2035, the proposed priorities include transitioning towards market driven procurement and achieving more than 40 per cent domestic value addition in BESS. Longer term recommendations extend to strengthening India's domestic value chain, expanding battery recycling and positioning the country as a supplier of energy storage technologies and expertise. High Dependence of PSP: A Worry Achieving the ambitious target of 888 GWh of energy storage capacity by 2035–36, including 567 GWh through Pumped Storage Projects (PSPs), may come with several challenges. Land acquisition, environmental and forest clearances, availability of suitable sites and water resources, and geological uncertainties could potentially delay project execution. PSPs involve high upfront investments, long construction periods and complex civil works, which may lead to cost overruns. Another major challenge could be ensuring the commercial viability of these projects. Uncertainty around storage tariffs, revenue models and returns on investment may make it difficult to attract private developers. Meanwhile, the remaining storage requirement will also depend on the expansion of battery energy storage systems, which face challenges related to domestic manufacturing capacity, critical mineral imports, battery costs and recycling. While India's storage ambitions are crucial for integrating higher renewable energy capacity into the grid, the real challenge will lie in translating the proposed project pipeline into financially viable and operational projects within the stipulated timeline.

stories.headline: Pia Dandiya secures Florida House seat in historic US Congress win
stories.title: Pia Dandiya secures Florida House seat in historic US Congress win
stories.summary: Washington, Nov 4: Pia Dandiya, the daughter of immigrants from Jaipur in Rajasthan, won Florida's 22nd Congressional District, becoming the second Indian American woman elected to the US House of Representatives, after Pramila Jayapal. Dandiya, a Democrat, defeated Republican businessman Casey Askar, according to projections by Decision Desk HQ and CBS News. NBC News showed a 'Projected winner' banner on the race, with Dandiya ahead by about 52 per cent to 48 per cent and about 99 per cent of the expected vote counted. NBC said the race shifted about 14 points towards Democrats compared with the 2024 presidential vote. Born and raised in Palm Beach County, Dandiya grew up in Jupiter, where her parents settled after emigrating from Jaipur in the 1980s. After moving to the US, her father, Dr Rohit Dandiya, continued his medical practice, while her mother, then 40, founded a Montessori school in Jupiter, initially established for Dandiya. Dandiya was raised with strong ties to her Indian heritage, and her parents sent her to India as a child to spend time with her cousins. "Very early on, my parents would send me on a solo trip to India to spend time with my cousins. These trips were life-changing and played a pivotal role in shaping my identity. They helped me understand how different democracies function and gave me a sense of global inequality," she told New India Abroad in an August 2025 interview. After her freshman year at Harvard, she spent a summer teaching English to children aged seven to 17 in the slums of New Delhi with the Asha Cooperative Society. "Teaching those underprivileged kids, I learnt what truly separates people from each other is not their potential, but their circumstances," she said. "I was born and raised in this district by parents who came to this country in pursuit of the American dream, and I've dedicated my career to making sure that dream is within reach for more families," Dandiya said when the Indian American Impact Fund endorsed her in 2025. Dandiya studied government at Harvard and earned a master's in education from Boston University. She taught with Teach For America in Boston and, at 28, became the founding principal of Democracy Prep Endurance High School in Harlem, where about 86 per cent of students were low-income, and every graduate was admitted to college, according to her campaign. "Around 86 per cent of students in my school lived below the poverty. But we promised them a brighter future: if they came to our school, 100 per cent of them would earn admission to college," she told New India Abroad. She was a White House Fellow in 2020, serving on the White House Domestic Policy Council and at the US Department of Education, and later led public-sector initiatives at Apple. Illinois Governor J.B. Pritzker appointed her to the state's P-20 Council. This was Dandiya's first run for office. She initially filed to run in the 21st District against Republican Brian Mast, then moved to the open 22nd District after Florida's mid-decade redistricting, and won the Democratic primary on August 18. The district leans Republican by registration, with about 1,85,000 Republicans, 1,46,000 Democrats and 1,50,000 voters with other affiliations, Florida Politics reported. Dandiya campaigned on the cost of living, corruption, healthcare, education and gun safety. "South Floridians are fed up with the rising costs and performative politics coming out of Washington," she told Florida Politics. The race drew heavy money. Through October 14, Dandiya raised about $4.6 million, while Askar raised about $7.4 million, most of it from loans to his own campaign. Askar's self-funding reached about $6.8 million, Federal Election Commission records show. No Going Back PAC, a super PAC funded by MAGA Inc., reported spending about $6.5 million against her by October 24, according to FEC filings. House Majority PAC, the main Democratic super PAC for House races, spent about $7.9 million against Askar. Dandiya won endorsements from the Indian American Impact Fund and Serve America PAC, and from Wellington's Republican mayor, Michael Napoleone. "I've always believed that the person matters more than the party, and Pia has earned my respect and my endorsement," Napoleone said. Former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg campaigned with her on October 26. The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee said on X that she "focused on the issues that matter most to South Florida -- addressing the affordability crisis and making sure that everyone has the opportunity to achieve the American Dream." "Congratulations to @PiaforCongress for winning her election! I am so excited to welcome the third South Asian American woman (along with me and @aishabbwahab) to the House!!!" Indian-American Representative Pramila Jayapal posted on X. Dandiya lives in Palm Beach Gardens with her husband, Navneet Alag, and their son, Sahib. Her win keeps the Indian-American "Samosa Caucus" in the House from shrinking in the new Congress. --IANS

stories.headline: SC upholds states’ power to levy additional sales tax, says case has become academic
stories.title: SC upholds states’ power to levy additional sales tax, says case has become academic
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 04: The Supreme Court on Wednesday held that a 1974 Constitution Bench ruling upholding states’ power to impose additional sales tax or surcharge calculated as a percentage of the existing sales tax continues to hold the field, saying a reference on the issue had become academic. A seven-judge Constitution bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant unanimously held that the legal question referred to it nearly 27 years ago no longer required adjudication, as the statutory provisions under challenge had since been replaced or amended and the Goods and Services Tax (GST) law had come into force. “The question referred to is of no practical significance and now academic. Consequently, the question referred to does not survive for adjudication by a seven-judge Bench, and the reference has to be answered accordingly,” the CJI, who wrote the judgment on behalf of himself and five other judges, said. The bench also comprised Justices K V Viswanathan, S V N Bhatti, Joymalya Bagchi, N V Anjaria, Arun Palli and V Mohana. Justice Viswanathan wrote a separate concurring verdict. While declining to undertake a fresh adjudication on the reference, the court clarified that the five-judge Constitution Bench ruling in S Kodar vs State of Kerala (1974) continued to hold the field. The earlier judgment had upheld additional sales tax, rejecting the argument that such a levy amounted to a tax on the income of dealers. “We have clarified that the case clearly held that an additional tax or surcharge computed as a percentage of the sales tax payable is an enhancement of the rate of sales tax and a tax on the sale or purchase of goods within Entry 54 of List II, as it then stood. That decision continues to hold the field,” the CJI said. The court further held that the question of the legislative competence of state legislatures to impose the surcharge would be governed by the law laid down in S Kodar. The detailed judgment is awaited. The reference arose from a challenge to Section 5A of the Orissa Sales Tax Act, 1947, which provided for additional tax at the rate of 10 per cent on dealers with an annual turnover between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore, and 15 per cent on dealers whose turnover exceeded Rs 1 crore. The appellants questioned whether the state legislature was competent to impose such a levy under Entry 54 of List II of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution, which empowered states to tax the sale or purchase of goods, or whether it effectively amounted to a tax on income, a subject falling within Parliament’s domain under Entry 82 of List I. The controversy stemmed from differing interpretations in earlier Supreme Court decisions. In S Kodar vs State of Kerala, a five-judge bench had upheld additional sales tax, ruling that a levy calculated with reference to the sales tax payable was an enhancement of the sales tax rate and not a tax on the dealer’s income. During the hearing on September 22, Solicitor General Tushar Mehta submitted that the controversy had largely become academic following the introduction of the GST regime in 2017, with relatively few disputes remaining pending.

stories.headline: Cabinet approves Rs 2,814 crore scheme to promote critical mineral processing
stories.title: Cabinet approves Rs 2,814 crore scheme to promote critical mineral processing
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 4: The Union Cabinet, chaired by the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, has approved the ‘Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing’ with a financial outlay of Rs.2,814 crore over a period of five years. Processing of critical minerals remains geographically concentrated in a few global locations. This exposes supply chains to geopolitical disruptions, price volatility, and potential supply restrictions, posing severe threats to supply chain resilience and economic security. This has implications for national security, economic sovereignty, and the timely achievement of decarbonisation targets. At present, India remains substantially dependent on imports for refined intermediates and high-purity materials, owing to the nascent stage of domestic beneficiation and processing infrastructure for critical minerals, including Lithium, Nickel, Cobalt. Domestic processing capacity for critical minerals remains limited, with commercial-scale projects facing challenges relating to high capital requirements, limited availability of suitable technologies and constrained access to raw materials. Domestic processing capacity is therefore imperative for maximising value addition, achieving import substitution, and establishing resilient end-to-end value chains. Against this backdrop, the “Capex Support Scheme to Promote Critical Mineral Processing” has been formulated to provide targeted capital expenditure support for the establishment and operationalisation of domestic processing facilities. The scheme aims to develop domestic processing capabilities in India to support value addition within the country, reduce import dependence, and develop value chain. The scheme targets processing of Lithium and Nickel ores/intermediary products into high purity compounds. Cobalt is also expected to be recovered as a by-product of nickel production. This will support critical sectors such as electric mobility, Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), electronics, defence, speciality steel etc. The proposed scheme envisages a total financial outlay of Rs.2,814 crore. The scheme period is from FY 2026-27 to 2030-31. Under the scheme, capital subsidy of 30% of eligible investment will be provided for setting up four critical mineral processing plants, comprising two lithium processing plants (with a minimum capacity of 30 kt each) and two nickel processing plants (with a minimum capacity of 50 kt each). The maximum capital support will be capped at Rs.500 crore per lithium beneficiary and Rs.900 crore per nickel beneficiary, respectively. The selection of beneficiaries shall be carried out through a two-stage process. In the first stage, applications shall be assessed for technical qualification, and only technically qualified applicants shall be eligible to participate in the second stage of financial bidding. For each mineral, two beneficiaries shall be selected based on the least-cost criterion, i.e., the lowest CAPEX support sought by the bidders under the Scheme. The incentives will be disbursed in three tranches linked to the achievement of specified milestones. The Scheme is an important step towards advancing the objectives of Atmanirbhar Bharat by supporting the development of resilient domestic processing infrastructure and strengthening India’s capabilities across the critical mineral value chain.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday (November 4) stayed the Madras High Court's order directing the constitution of a five-member Board of Management to take over the administration of the Chidambaram Nataraja Temple from the Podhu Dikshitars.
A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul Pancholi passed the interim order while hearing the challenge filed by the temple's Podhu Dikshitars against the High Court's direction.

The Madras High Court had passed the order on October 30, 2026, while disposing of a batch of writ petitions concerning the administration of the Sri Sabanayagar Temple, popularly known as the Chidambaram Nataraja Temple, in Tamil Nadu.

A Division Bench of Justice G Jayachandran and Justice E Manoharan had constituted the Board of Management, holding that judicial intervention was necessary to address alleged maladministration of the temple.

The five-member board was to comprise retired Madras High Court judge Justice V Bharathidasan as Chairman, retired judge Justice R Suresh Kumar as Co-Chairman, and retired IAS officer C Rajendran as a member.
The Secretary of the Podhu Dikshitars and the Secretary of the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department were to serve as ex-officio members.
The High Court had directed the board to take over the temple's administration "till the ill is cured".
The board was tasked with overseeing the temple's properties, financial accounts, heritage conservation and other administrative affairs.

It was also directed to take steps to retrieve encroached temple properties, recover rental arrears, maintain proper accounts and ensure equal opportunities for devotees to have darshan from the Kanagasabai.

However, the High Court had clarified that the daily rituals and periodical festivals would remain within the exclusive prerogative of the Podhu Dikshitars, subject to established customs and practices.

The High Court's order had been challenged before the Supreme Court by the Podhu Dikshitars, who contended that the direction interfered with their right to administer the temple under Article 26 of the Constitution.

Police under Section 163 Bharatiya Nagarik Duraksha Sanhita (BNSS) in the national capital show restrictions concerning free movement were imposed way before protests erupted demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.

Six orders issued on August 20 or immediately before or after this date, came a month after the July 20 protests against alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leaks witnessed violence in New Delhi district, the power and commercial heart of the capital city.

stories.title: Supreme Court Refuses To Relax Practice Condition For Court Staff To Join Judicial Service

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday declined to grant a one-time relaxation of the mandatory practice requirement for in-service court employees seeking entry into the judicial service, orally observing that judicial posts cannot be treated as a promotional avenue for other cadres.

A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, along with Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana, dismissed applications filed by court staff who had approached the Court seeking modification of the Bhumika Trust judgment, which waived the practice condition for graduates till March 31, 2027.
The applicants, 21 officers from Karnataka sought relaxation for Court staff as well.

Senior Advocate Aditya Sondhi, appearing for the applicants, submitted that different States were applying the Court's earlier judgment in the Bhumika Trust case inconsistently with respect to in-service candidates.

He pointed out that Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Maharashtra continued to permit recruitment by transfer for in-service persons, while Karnataka insisted that such candidates must compete in the open category.

CJI Surya Kant responded that the creation of a separate channel was a matter for the States under Article 309 or through legislation, but the Court would not issue a direction to introduce another mode of recruitment.
“That is for the State.
They can exercise their power under Article 309, or perhaps through legislation.
But we would like to keep ourselves away from issuing a direction that they should introduce another channel of recruitment,” the Chief Justice said.
Sondhi argued that persons in service in Karnataka were being hit by the rules after the High Court, in exercise of its administrative powers, relied on the Supreme Court's judgment.
“I am willing to compete.
In Karnataka, until 2026, in-service candidates were permitted,” he submitted.

stories.title: Supreme Court Asks MP Speaker To Decide Congress Leader's Disqualification Petition Against Nirmala Sapre MLA In 2 Months

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday directed the Speaker of the Madhya Pradesh Legislative Assembly to decide within two months a pending disqualification petition against Bina MLA Nirmala Sapre under the anti-defection law.

The petition, filed in July 2024 by Congress Leader of Opposition Umang Singhar, alleges that Sapre voluntarily gave up her membership of the Indian National Congress, the party on whose ticket she was elected in the 2023 Assembly polls, and joined the BJP.

Senior Advocate Vivek Tankha, appearing for the petitioner, described it as a “classic case” under the Tenth Schedule, stating that Sapre had left the party and was campaigning with the opposite side, yet the Speaker had not commenced proceedings.

The bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana hearing the matter noted the allegations of voluntary relinquishment of party membership triggering disqualification under the Tenth Schedule.
It observed that the petition had remained undecided for over two years.

The Madhya Pradesh High Court had earlier dismissed Singhar's plea seeking a time-bound decision, holding that there was no urgency as proceedings were underway and Sapre had denied resigning from Congress or joining the BJP.
The Supreme Court disagreed with the High Court's approach on urgency.

It held that even where a court finds no immediate urgency, or where considerable time remains until the Assembly's term expires, petitions under the Tenth Schedule must still be decided expeditiously.
The Court therefore directed the Speaker to decide the disqualification petition within two months.
The Court also cited its precedent in Padi Kaushik Reddy which set a deadline to the Telangana Speaker to decide disqualification petitions.
Sapre, a first-time MLA from Bina in Sagar district, had won the seat on a Congress ticket in 2023.
In May 2024, during the Lok Sabha election campaign, she appeared on a BJP platform in the presence of Chief Minister Mohan Yadav and announced her decision to join the ruling party.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Rejects Plea To Rotate SC/ST Reservations Of Assembly & Parliament Seats, Affirms Validity Of S.9(1)(c) Delimitation Act
stories.title: Supreme Court Rejects Plea To Rotate SC/ST Reservations Of Assembly & Parliament Seats, Affirms Validity Of S.9(1)(c) Delimitation Act
stories.summary: The Court declined interference, observing that it was a matter of legislative policy.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court declined interference, observing that it was a matter of legislative policy.

The Supreme Court on Wednesday rejected a plea seeking mandatory rotation of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in State Legislative Assemblies and Parliament, holding that the issue falls within the legislative domain of Parliament and cannot be directed by the courts.

The Court was dealing with a petition challenging Section 9(1)(c) of the Delimitation Act, 2002, which requires reserved constituencies to be located in areas where the proportion of SC/ST population is comparatively large.
After the Allahabad High Court upheld Section 9(1)(c) and refused to order rotation of reserved seats, the petitioner approached the Supreme Court.

The bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana refused to interfere with the High Court's judgment, observing that it was a matter for the legislature to decide.
The Court allowed the petitioner to file a representation before the elected representatives seeking a change in the law.

The petitioner, Jagdish Singh, an elector of the 191-Kadipur Assembly Constituency in Sultanpur district of Uttar Pradesh, had argued that the seat had remained reserved for SCs for nearly seven decades since its creation.

He contended that the continuous reservation without rotation violated Articles 14, 15 and 19 of the Constitution, diluted the right to vote by compelling voters to choose only from SC candidates, and benefited only a few families rather than the broader community.
He sought a system of rotation similar to that provided for panchayats and municipalities under Articles 243D and 243T.
During the hearing, the bench observed that voters in a multiparty democracy are expected to vote on the basis of political ideology rather than caste or religion.

Justice Bagchi noted that whether concentrating reserved seats in areas with larger SC/ST populations creates caste divisions is a matter for the legislature to examine and does not by itself render the law unconstitutional.

The Court distinguished the constitutional right to vote from any claimed right to contest from a particular constituency, pointing out that general-category candidates can contest from non-reserved seats.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Asks Centre To Create Special Cell To Monitor Enforcement Of Child Labour Prohibition Act
stories.title: Supreme Court Asks Centre To Create Special Cell To Monitor Enforcement Of Child Labour Prohibition Act
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently directed the Secretary of the Ministry of Women and Child Development to constitute a special cell to monitor the implementation of the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, as amended in 2016, and ensure strict compliance with its provisions.
The Court also directed the Centre to issue instructions to enforcement agencies through the respective Chief Secretaries of States to ensure effective implementation of the law.

A bench comprising Justice SVN Bhatti and Justice NV Anjaria passed the directions while disposing of a writ petition challenging the provisions of the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, particularly Section 3, which originally prohibited the employment of children only in specified hazardous occupations.

The petition was disposed of after the Court took note of the 2016 amendment to the Act, which introduced a blanket prohibition on the employment of children below 14 years of age in all occupations and processes, subject to limited exceptions.
The amendment permits children to assist in non-hazardous family enterprises after school hours or during vacations, subject to the statutory conditions.
The bench observed that the prayers raised in the writ petition no longer survived for consideration in view of the legislative changes.
However, it emphasised that the effective implementation of the amended law remained a responsibility of the authorities.
"We take note of the writ prayers, the orders passed by this Court and also the amendment to the parent Act.

We are of the view that the prayer, as made, in the writ petition does not survive for further consideration but what remains to be taken note of is giving complete and full effect to the changes introduced by way of amendment Act No. 35 of 2016.

Keeping in perspective the above brief narrative, we are persuaded not to examine the prayers as made but we take note of the amendment Act No. 35 of 2016 and note that it shall be the responsibility of the respondent(s) to ensure complete and strict compliance of the mandate of the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986 including the amended provisions.

For the said purpose, with a view to preserving the rights of children/ adolescents, we direct the second respondent to constitute a special cell, continue to monitor the implementation of the provisions of the Act and also issue directions to the enforcing agencies through the respective Chief Secretaries of the State, as amended through the Act No.35 of 2016."
